title: Global Financial Stability Report, October 2026, Chapter 1: Beneath the Resilience: Rising Risks, Unresolved Vulnerabilities
key_claim: Among 10 BDCs with $300 billion in total assets, 4, representing about $90 billion in assets, have commitments to borrowers that exceed their available liquidity buffers; semi-liquid vehicles supplied more than 50 percent of new US direct lending fundraising in 2025 before the redemption wave.
frame_summary: Argues that the liquidity risk in direct lending is widening from investor redemptions to contingent commitments to borrowers, which could turn fund liquidity pressure into a contraction in credit supply.
verbatim_quote: among 10 BDCs with $300 billion in total assets, 4—representing about $90 billion in assets—have commitments exceeding their available liquidity buffers
verbatim_list: Direct lending funds—across retail- and institutional-focused vehicles—increasingly provide borrowers with substantial contingent liquidity commitments.

Although most of these funds appear to be able to manage investor redemptions,
In a stress scenario, borrowers could draw heavily on these facilities just as funds’ own liquidity resources are eroded by lower collateral values.

title: Global Financial Markets Face Rising Risks From AI, Bond Yields, and Cyberattacks

frame_summary: Argues that borrower draws on direct-lending commitments could arrive just as the lending funds face their own liquidity pressure, and that banks' exposures to private credit need sectoral capital and concentration limits.

title: The Price of Bank Funding Behind Private Credit: Evidence from Business Development Companies (FEDS Notes)
key_claim: By the end of the 2012Q3-2023Q4 sample, bank commitments to BDCs exceeded $60 billion, nearly 90 percent of it credit lines; during the 2022 tightening BDC credit-line utilization rose 14.2 percentage points more than for other borrowers and banks charged a premium of roughly 1.1 percentage points; the top ten banks hold more than 80 percent of committed lending to BDCs.
frame_summary: Argues that private credit is not separate from banks because BDCs rely on bank credit lines, that BDCs drew more on those lines during the 2022 tightening, and that the funding market is concentrated in a few banks.
verbatim_quote: By the end of the sample, total bank commitments to BDCs reported in the Y-14 data exceeded $60 billion. In dollar-weighted terms, nearly 90 percent of bank lending to BDCs takes the form of credit lines.
verbatim_list: BDC credit-line utilization rose by 14.2 percentage points more
Taken together, the BDC interest-rate premium reached roughly 1.1 percentage points during the tightening cycle.
the top ten account for more than 80 percent

title: Why Semi-Liquid Private Credit Funds Are in Fragile Territory
key_claim: Reporting the Fang, Goldstein and Zeng paper on 52 semi-liquid BDCs: Q2 2026 repurchase outflows of $7.1 billion against $3.8 billion of issuance, the first aggregate net outflow in the funds' history, with $10.7 billion of requests left unmet by the 5% cap and average cash of 5.5% of net assets.
frame_summary: Argues that redemption caps do not remove the cost of turning illiquid loans into liquid investor claims, so funds fall back on loan sales, leverage and delayed payments in a leverage-redemption loop.
verbatim_quote: In the second quarter of 2026, indeed, repurchase outflows from semi-liquid BDCs reached $7.1 billion, while issuance inflows dwindled to $3.8 billion, resulting in aggregate net outflows from semi-liquid BDCs for the first time in their history, the paper notes.
verbatim_list: an increasing amount, $10.7 billion, of redemption requests has been left unmet, or “gated,” by the 5% cap
Semi-liquid BDCs have cash holdings of only an average 5.5% of total net assets, or TNA.

title: Goldman Sachs private credit BDC redemptions come in below 5% again in Q3

frame_summary: Reports that redemption pressure is easing at the best-placed non-traded BDC while staying elevated across the industry.
